examples: `new Sheet` stores six values and calls nothing; a program meets a `Sheet` from `Workbook::addSheet`, and the examples of that method and of `addRow` show how a sheet is started and filled.
perf: `new Sheet` stores six values and calls nothing; `Workbook::addSheet` builds one on every call, so its figure includes this one.
hostile: `new Sheet` stores six typed read-only values and calls nothing, so a wrong value does not compile; the rows and parts a request sends reach the sheet through `addRow` and the part methods, whose attacks send hostile ones.
